{{Ritual ceremonies of the Imperial Palace}}
{{nihongo||皇霊祭|'''Kōreisai'''}}, or {{nihongo||春季|Shun-ki|Vernal}} and {{nihongo||秋季|Shū-ki|Autumnal}} Kōreisai, are days of worship in {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}} that began in 1878 to pay respects to the {{ill|List of emperors of Japan|en|List of emperors of Japan|qid=Q188210|lt=past emperors|1=List of emperors of Japan}} and {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|en|Imperial House of Japan|qid=Q909452|lt=imperial family members|1=Imperial House of Japan}}. It occurred on the {{ill|March equinox|en|March equinox|qid=Q12889843|lt=March equinox|1=March equinox}} (spring equinox) and the {{ill|September equinox|en|September equinox|qid=Q7530126|lt=September equinox|1=September equinox}} (autumn equinox) of the anniversary of the person's death. After the 1948 passing of the Act on National Holidays, these days were marked in a non-religious manner as the {{ill|Public holidays in Japan|en|Public holidays in Japan|qid=Q1195354|lt=national holidays|1=Public holidays in Japan}} of {{ill|Vernal Equinox Day|en|Vernal Equinox Day|qid=Q1049141|lt=Vernal Equinox Day|1=Vernal Equinox Day}} and {{ill|Autumnal Equinox Day|en|Autumnal Equinox Day|qid=Q1186410|lt=Autumnal Equinox Day|1=Autumnal Equinox Day}}. During the event, one prayed for good harvest in the spring and said {{ill|Harvest festival|en|Harvest festival|qid=Q2304773|lt=thank you for the harvest|1=Harvest festival}} in autumn.  The equinoxes were also the days of {{ill|Ancestor veneration in China|en|Ancestor veneration in China|qid=Q4752556|lt=Ancestor veneration in China|1=Ancestor veneration in China}}.<ref>https://web.archive.org/web/20231209040242/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9100</ref>
